import numpy as np
def pairs_panel(seed=2006, n_ind=10, per_ind=10, n_pairs=20, days=3024, half_life=8.0, ou_sd=0.008,
                rw_sd=0.015, break_day=1512, break_frac=0.8, half_spread=0.005):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    N = n_ind * per_ind
    ind = np.repeat(np.arange(n_ind), per_ind)
    mkt = np.cumsum(0.0003 + 0.010 * rng.standard_normal(days))
    indf = np.cumsum(0.008 * rng.standard_normal((days, n_ind)), axis=0)
    phi = 0.5 ** (1.0 / half_life)
    u = np.cumsum(rw_sd * rng.standard_normal((days, N)), axis=0)        # unpaired: random walks
    common = np.cumsum(rw_sd * rng.standard_normal((days, n_pairs)), axis=0)
    eps = ou_sd * rng.standard_normal((days, 2 * n_pairs))
    a = np.zeros((days, 2 * n_pairs))
    for t in range(1, days):
        a[t] = phi * a[t - 1] + eps[t]                                   # mean-reverting gaps
    broken = rng.random(n_pairs) < break_frac
    drift = np.cumsum(rw_sd * rng.standard_normal((days, 2 * n_pairs)), axis=0)
    for k in range(n_pairs):
        for j in (2 * k, 2 * k + 1):
            x = common[:, k] + a[:, j]
            if broken[k]:                                                # the pair stops co-moving
                x = x + np.where(np.arange(days) >= break_day, drift[:, j] - drift[break_day, j], 0.0)
            u[:, j] = x
    pair_ind = np.repeat(np.arange(n_ind), 2)[:n_pairs]
    ind[:2 * n_pairs] = np.repeat(pair_ind, 2)                           # two planted pairs an industry
    logp = np.log(50.0) + mkt[:, None] + indf[:, ind] + u
    mid = np.exp(logp)
    bounce = np.where(rng.random((days, N)) < 0.5, 1 + half_spread, 1 - half_spread)
    close = mid * bounce                                                 # closes at bid or ask
    return close, mid, ind, broken


def normalise(P):
    P = np.asarray(P, dtype=float)
    return P / P[0]


def ssd_matrix(Pn):
    G = Pn.T @ Pn
    d = np.diag(G)
    return d[:, None] + d[None, :] - 2 * G


def top_pairs(Pn, k):
    D = ssd_matrix(Pn)
    i, j = np.triu_indices(D.shape[0], 1)
    order = np.argsort(D[i, j], kind="stable")[:k]
    return [(int(i[o]), int(j[o])) for o in order]


def trade_pair(form, trade, i, j, wait=0, open_at=2.0):
    sd = float(np.std(form[:, i] - form[:, j]))
    a, b = trade[:, i].tolist(), trade[:, j].tolist()
    n = len(a)
    payoff, opened, t = 0.0, False, 0
    while t < n:
        s = a[t] - b[t]
        if sd > 0 and abs(s) > open_at * sd and t + wait < n - 1:
            side = 1 if s > 0 else -1          # +1: i is dearer, so short i and buy j
            to = t + wait
            tc = next((u for u in range(t + 1, n) if (a[u] - b[u]) * side <= 0), None)
            tx = n - 1 if tc is None else min(tc + wait, n - 1)
            ri = (a[tx] - a[to]) / a[to]
            rj = (b[tx] - b[to]) / b[to]
            payoff += side * (rj - ri)
            opened = True
            t = tx + 1
            continue
        t += 1
    return payoff, opened


def trade_trips(form, trade, i, j, wait=0, open_at=2.0):
    """Every round trip of trade_pair as (open day, close day, converged, payoff)."""
    sd = float(np.std(form[:, i] - form[:, j]))
    a, b = trade[:, i].tolist(), trade[:, j].tolist()
    n = len(a)
    trips, t = [], 0
    while t < n:
        s = a[t] - b[t]
        if sd > 0 and abs(s) > open_at * sd and t + wait < n - 1:
            side = 1 if s > 0 else -1
            to = t + wait
            tc = next((u for u in range(t + 1, n) if (a[u] - b[u]) * side <= 0), None)
            tx = n - 1 if tc is None else min(tc + wait, n - 1)
            pay = side * ((b[tx] - b[to]) / b[to] - (a[tx] - a[to]) / a[to])
            trips.append((to, tx, tc is not None, pay))
            t = tx + 1
            continue
        t += 1
    return trips


def cycle_return(close, start, k, wait=0, open_at=2.0):
    """(committed, employed, opened) for the k closest pairs of the cycle from day start."""
    Pn = normalise(close[start:start + 378])
    form, trade = Pn[:252], Pn[252:]
    res = [trade_pair(form, trade, i, j, wait, open_at) for i, j in top_pairs(form, k)]
    total = sum(p for p, _ in res)
    n = sum(1 for _, o in res if o)
    return total / k, (total / n if n else 0.0), n


def run(close, k, wait=0, step=21, open_at=2.0):
    """[(start, committed return over the six trading months)] for every cycle."""
    return [(s, cycle_return(close, s, k, wait, open_at)[0]) for s in range(0, close.shape[0] - 378 + 1, step)]

close, mid, ind, broken = pairs_panel()

screens.title: Two measures of a decline
screens.prose:
We measured the decline in two ways. One compares returns; the other asks why they fell:
$$\text{survived} = \frac{\bar r_{\text{after}}}{\bar r_{\text{before}}}, \qquad c = \frac{\text{trades closed at a crossing}}{\text{trades opened}}$$
A fall in $c$ says pairs stopped co-moving, not that gaps closed faster.

hints.text: After over before.
About 42%.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Divide after by before.

explain.text: 0.48% / 1.14% is about 42%, close to the same-day 42%. Waiting a day lowers both halves by a similar share. Lesson 14 tests this split as an out-of-sample result.

screens.title: A quarterly review
screens.prose: You run a book of 40 equity pairs. Over four quarters its hit rate, the share of trades closed at a crossing, fell from 72% to 51%. The number of trades held at about 60 a quarter.

Widen the entry threshold to 3 sd so fewer trades open
options.why: That treats a pair problem as a threshold problem. Broken pairs fail at any threshold.

options.text: Conclude the trade is crowded and close the book
options.why: Crowding predicts gaps that close sooner, not trades that stop closing.

options.text: Double the size of each trade to restore the P&L
options.why: Larger trades on pairs that no longer converge lose more.

hints.text: What does a falling hit rate with steady trade counts say?
Trades still open; fewer come back.
That points at the pairs, so test them one by one.

feedback.generic: Not quite. A falling crossing share points at the pairs themselves.

explain.text: A steady trade count with fewer crossings is the pattern of broken pairs, as in our panel. Test each live pair on recent data and drop those whose spreads drift. Then recheck the hit rate on what is left.
